title: Best Lunch Boxes UK
short: Bento, sandwich and salad lunch boxes and a lunch bag compared on how well they actually seal, from an £8 salad box to a leakproof favourite.
intro: A lunch box's real test is whether it survives a commute without oozing into your bag. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested lunchbox roundup, where each box was used and reviewed for seal, size and build. That guide has been archived and dates from April 2023, so prices are as reviewed and may have changed. For plain leftovers containers, see our food storage containers guide.

products.name: Panino
products.best_for: Commuters who pack a sandwich, sides and a dip together
products.key_spec: Four compartments under one moulded silicone lid, 22 x 15 x 5cm, 490g, BPA-free
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this the most ooze-proof box they tried, with a single moulded silicone lid sealing four compartments from each other so yoghurt, hummus or sauce in the middle can't leak into the rest. The seal wasn't 100% waterproof, so drinks need a separate container, and the silicone means it lasts longer if the outer box is hand-washed.
pros: Four sealed compartments keep foods apart
BPA-free and phthalates-free, dishwasher-safe inner tray
cons: Seal isn't 100% waterproof, so keep drinks separate
Outer box should be hand-washed for a longer life
Bright colours may not suit a boardroom lunch

products.name: Sandwich Box
products.best_for: Buyers who want a stylish, plastic-light box for a proper sandwich
products.key_spec: Stainless steel box, bamboo lid that doubles as a chopping board, silicone seal, elastic band, 22 x 15 x 5cm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this roomier than it looks, as big as the Yumbox, with room for a sizeable sandwich plus nibbles. The silicone seal helps prevent spillages and the bamboo lid works as a chopping board, but the elastic band closure feels less secure than a clip lid and the lid isn't dishwasher safe.
pros: Roomy for a sandwich plus sides
Bamboo lid doubles as a chopping board
cons: Elastic band feels less secure than a clip lid

products.name: Organic Cotton Zipper Lunch Bag
products.best_for: Buyers who want a washable, eco-friendly bag that looks like a handbag
products.key_spec: Double-layer organic cotton with polyester lining, machine-washable, stretchy inner pocket, nine patterns
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this beautifully made and washable, with thick organic cotton and a water-safe lining that helps keep food warm or cold, plus a robust zip and stitching. The price is steep for a bag and you wouldn't put sandwiches straight in without wrapping them, but it could cut lunch spending for years.
pros: Cotton and lining help keep food warm or cold
Stretchy inner pocket fits a small flask
cons: Steep price for a lunch bag
Food should be wrapped rather than placed loose inside

products.name: Original Bento
products.best_for: Big appetites who want two full lunch-size boxes in one
products.key_spec: Two stackable 600ml boxes, clip lids with silicone border, elastic band, cutlery included
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this classic stackable bento, effectively two 600ml boxes, roomy enough to take seconds to work, and one of the most durable boxes on their list, with proper plastic cutlery included. It could be better engineered: the internal separators don't fit snugly, the pieces only stay together with the elastic band, and the wood-effect plastic feels plasticky.
pros: Big capacity, two 600ml boxes in one
One of the most durable boxes tested
cons: Parts don't stay together without the elastic band

products.name: Salad To Go
products.best_for: Anyone taking a salad to work on a small budget
products.key_spec: 1.1L BPA-free plastic, KLIP-IT locking clips, dressing compartment, knife and fork included
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this classic budget salad box keeps leaves from going soggy thanks to a separate dressing compartment, and it includes a knife and fork. It's microwave, freezer and dishwasher safe, but the flexible seal isn't leakproof, so they wouldn't recommend carrying soup in it.
pros: Dressing compartment keeps salad from going soggy
cons: Flexible seal isn't leakproof, so not for soup

guide.q: Which type of lunch box should I choose?
guide.a: A bento box, like the Umami here, separates food into compartments or tiers. A sandwich box, like the Black+Blum, has room for bread with space for fruit or a yoghurt beside it. A lunch bag suits softer packing, though it won't protect food from being squashed. For soup, Expert Reviews recommends an insulated food flask instead, as flasks are more watertight than boxes calling themselves leakproof.

guide.q: What is the best lunch box material?
guide.a: Good polypropylene plastic is durable, light, cheap and safe in the dishwasher, microwave and freezer, but check it's BPA-free. Silicone seals prevent leaks but wear faster in dishwashers. Stainless steel is naturally antibacterial and durable, and bamboo is attractive but warps and stains easily so is best used for lids.

guide.q: How leakproof are lunch boxes really?
guide.a: It varies, and labels can overstate it. In Expert Reviews' testing the Yumbox Panino was the most ooze-proof, but even it wasn't fully waterproof, and the Sistema Salad To Go's flexible seal wasn't leakproof. Keep drinks and soups in a separate container or flask.

guide.q: Are cheap takeaway-style plastic boxes worth it?
guide.a: Expert Reviews advises against them: they're little better than single-use plastic, typically can't go in the dishwasher, freezer or microwave, may not be BPA-free, and aren't leakproof. A properly made box costs more but lasts far longer and cuts single-use plastic waste.
